# Week 02: R for Data Analytics

## Part 1: Understanding Data Types

```{r}
# Numeric (continuous) variables
age <- 25
height <- 175.5

# Integer variables
year <- 2025L

# Character (string) variables
name <- "John Doe"

# Logical (boolean) variables
is_student <- TRUE

# Factor (categorical) variables
education_level <- factor(c("High School", "Bachelor", "Master", "PhD"))
grade <- factor(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "F"), ordered = TRUE)

# Check variable types
cat("Type of age:", class(age), "\n")
```


```{r}
# Categorical Variables

# 1. Binary variable example: Pass/Fail
pass_fail <- c("Pass", "Fail", "Pass", "Pass", "Fail")
pass_fail_factor <- factor(pass_fail)

cat("Binary variable levels:", levels(pass_fail_factor), "\n")


# 2. Nominal: Categories without order
departments <- factor(c("HR", "IT", "Finance", "Marketing", "IT", "HR", "Finance"))

cat("Department frequency:\n")
table(departments)

# 3. Ordinal: Categories with logical order
satisfaction <- factor(
  c("Very Unsatisfied", "Unsatisfied", "Neutral", "Satisfied", "Very Satisfied",
    "Satisfied", "Neutral", "Very Satisfied", "Satisfied", "Unsatisfied"),
  levels = c("Very Unsatisfied", "Unsatisfied", "Neutral", "Satisfied", "Very Satisfied"),
  ordered = TRUE
)

cat("Satisfaction levels:\n")
```


```{r}
# Continuous Variables

# 1. Interval: Equal intervals but no true zero (e.g., temperature in Celsius)
temperatures <- c(15, 18, 22, 25, 20, 16, 19, 23, 21, 17) # Note: 0°C doesn't mean "no temperature"

# 2. Ratio: Equal intervals AND true zero (e.g., height, weight, income)
heights <- c(160, 175, 182, 168, 155, 190, 172, 165, 178, 185)
```



## Part 2: Descriptive Analytics

```{r}
# Descriptive analysis summarizes and describes the main features of a dataset using measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and measures of spread (variance, standard deviation, range). It provides an overview of what the data looks like through summary statistics without making inferences or predictions beyond the data itself. Common tools include frequency distributions, summary tables, and basic visualizations like histograms and bar charts.
```
